summary: Creates and deletes replicated operator copies from a master operator, driven either by a table row set or a numeric count, with naming, destination, maximum-count, layout, and callback scripting controls.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Replicate By Number or By Table

key_params.name: numreplicants
key_params.note: Number of copies when using By Number

key_params.name: template
key_params.note: Template table whose rows drive copies when using By Table

key_params.name: namefromtable
key_params.note: Generate names from row index, column index, or column name

key_params.name: ignorefirstrow
key_params.note: Skip the first table row, often used as a header

key_params.name: colname
key_params.note: Column name used for table-driven naming

key_params.name: colindex
key_params.note: Column index used for table-driven naming

key_params.name: destination
key_params.note: Network where replicated operators are placed

key_params.name: tscript
key_params.note: Callback script DAT for per-replicant behavior

key_concepts: Replicator COMP creates and deletes operator copies from a master by table rows or by a numeric count.
Table-driven replication can name copies by row index, column index, or a column name, with optional header-row skipping.
Master, destination, and maximum-operator parameters define the replication scope and safety boundary.
The master and replicants do not need to be components or clones, though a self-cloned master can create cloned replicants.
Callback/script customization can modify each replicant, and unchanged table rows are not recreated when only one row changes.
common_gotchas: Destination cannot be blank; use . for inside the Replicator COMP or .. for alongside it in the parent.
The master can be a full component or a single operator and does not have to be a clone master.
Replicator COMP creates and deletes nodes as the table or count changes; do not manually edit generated nodes unless callbacks preserve those edits.
If only one table line changes, unchanged replicants are not recreated, which is useful but can surprise callbacks that assume full rebuilds.
Removing onRemoveReplicant() can keep removed replicants around for reuse, so stale state must be cleared explicitly.
Name-from-table values must be valid and unique operator names after prefixing or replication can collide.
